gaps.sentence: The ancient scrolls are far too brittle ___ .
gaps.explanation: The scrolls receive the action: passive infinitive to be + unrolled.

gaps.sentence: The museum ___ (close) to the public on Mondays.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: is + closed. No agent needed; the routine is what matters.

gaps.sentence: The road ___ (resurface) at the time, so we took the coast route instead.
gaps.hint: in progress at a past moment
gaps.explanation: 'At the time' requires past continuous passive: was being + resurfaced.

gaps.sentence: All the passwords ___ (reset) after last week's security breach.
gaps.hint: recent past, plural subject, present relevance
gaps.explanation: Present perfect passive: have been + reset for a recently completed action.

gaps.sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
gaps.explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.

gaps.sentence: He had his wisdom tooth ___ (take out) yesterday morning.
gaps.explanation: Causative: had + his wisdom tooth + taken out. The particle 'out' stays with the participle.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript is too fragile ___ (handle) without gloves.
gaps.explanation: Passive to-infinitive: to be + past participle. The manuscript receives the handling.

gaps.sentence: The stolen car ___ (find) abandoned in a car park this morning.
gaps.explanation: 'This morning' (now over) takes past simple passive: was + found.
